name: Zellberg
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village above Zell am Ziller, featuring traditional architecture and a breathtaking view of the Zillertal mountain range.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Zellberg is situated in the central Zillertal valley within the Tyrolean district of Schwaz, clinging to the sun-soaked slopes of the Tux Alps directly west and above Zell am Ziller. The municipal territory stretches from the valley floor along the river Ziller at Zellbergeben at around 575 metres, through the village centre at 770 metres, up to alpine pastures and rugged peaks above 2,000 metres. Approximately 650 residents live in this scenic mountain community, defined by traditional timber farmsteads, scattered hamlets, and sustainable dairy farming. Zellberg is widely celebrated as a dramatic access gate to the Zillertaler Höhenstraße panoramic road and as the home of the renowned folk music group Zellberg Buam.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement of these sunny mountain terraces began in the High Middle Ages with Bavarian and Alemannic farmers clearing the forests. Zellberg was first documented in 1318. For centuries, life revolved around demanding alpine agriculture on steep inclines, supported by the favourable south-eastern sun exposure. In 1891, local mountain farmers built the neo-Gothic Sacred Heart Chapel (Herz-Jesu-Kapelle) as a spiritual votive sanctuary. In the early 1960s, construction commenced on the Zillertaler Höhenstraße high alpine road as an agricultural route, with the steep access ramp from Zell am Ziller across Zellberg opening to tourism in 1978, gradually fostering gentle alpine tourism.

Anreise

Travel to Zellberg leads through the Zillertal valley. Leaving the Inntal motorway A12 at junction Wiesing/Zillertal, drivers take the federal highway B169 to Zell am Ziller. From there, the well-paved Zellberg provincial road L229 winds up through switchbacks to the village centre and onward to high-altitude farms and the toll-paying Zillertaler Höhenstraße. Rail passengers travel to Jenbach and switch to the Zillertalbahn to Zell am Ziller. From the railway station, local taxis and buses head up into Zellberg, while seasonal panorama buses run in summer all the way to Hirschbichlalm and Melchboden.

Tipps

The Zillertaler Höhenstraße is the supreme local attraction: this alpine panoramic road ascends from Zellberg to altitudes over 2,000 metres, offering breathtaking vistas plunging down into the valley floor and reaching towards glaciated summits. Along the road sits the historic Hirschbichlalm inn at 1,840 metres, famous for hearty Tyrolean dishes and folk music gatherings. Visitors can hike to the charming Sacred Heart Chapel along the educational timber theme trail (Holzweg). For ambitious hikers, the Rastkogelhütte at 2,124 metres serves as a base to ascend the 2,762-metre Rastkogel peak.
